title: XLOOKUP not-found vs IFERROR
summary: Learn what the XLOOKUP fourth argument catches, what IFERROR catches, and when to use each.

blocks.text: A planner at head office is calculating sell-through for products in a store: units sold divided by opening stock. The product list has a code, the opening stock and the units sold. Some codes in the store file are not on the list, and one new product has stock of zero.

Two different tools handle problems. XLOOKUP has its own fourth argument for a missing code. IFERROR wraps any formula and replaces any error. They catch different things, so you need to know which one to use.

items: Objective: choose between the if_not_found argument and IFERROR, and use IFERROR to protect a calculation built on lookups.
You pass the mission at 75% or more in the Assessment.

blocks.text: The fourth argument is used only when the code is not found. It does not catch any other error.
IFERROR shows value unless value is an error of any kind (#N/A, #DIV/0!, #VALUE! and others). In that case it shows value_if_error instead.

blocks.caption: What each tool catches
rows: Code is missing, so XLOOKUP gives #N/A
Divide by zero (#DIV/0!) in the next step
A mistake in your own formula, such as the wrong range
Yes, which can hide the mistake

blocks.text: ZZ-999 is not on the list, so the cell shows the text Not listed. The text is a good clear message, but you cannot use it in arithmetic.
If C2 is zero, D2/C2 would show #DIV/0!. If C2 holds the text Not listed, it would show #VALUE!. IFERROR replaces both with n/a.

items: Use if_not_found when you only want to handle a missing code and want other errors to stay visible.
Use IFERROR to protect a calculation that can fail in several ways, such as a division.
Be careful: IFERROR hides every error, including a typing mistake in your own formula. Use it on the calculation you know can fail, not on every cell.

blocks.text: Use the formulas and table from Training. Give decimals to 2 decimal places if needed.

items: The XLOOKUP fourth argument handles one problem only: the code is not found.
IFERROR replaces any error from the formula inside it, such as #DIV/0! or #VALUE!.
Text such as Not listed cannot be used in arithmetic, so wrap calculations in IFERROR.
IFERROR can hide real mistakes, so use it on purpose, not on every cell.

blocks.text: Use the lookup argument for missing codes and IFERROR for calculations that can fail.

items.prompt: The code GB-610 is on the list, but its opening stock is 0. In the sheet, C2 holds that stock (0) and D2 holds the units sold, so D2/C2 shows #DIV/0!. Which tool replaces this #DIV/0! with n/a?
ZZ-999 is not on the list. What does =XLOOKUP("ZZ-999",$G$2:$G$6,$H$2:$H$6,"Not listed")*2 show?
A product has opening stock of 48 and units sold of 36. Give the sell-through (units sold divided by opening stock) as a decimal, for example 0.5.
Why is it risky to wrap every formula on a sheet in IFERROR(..., "n/a")?

options.label: It also hides real mistakes, such as a wrong range, so the problem is not noticed
